entries.message:
Hi everyone!
By turning this channel into an ideas hub, we lost the process where the support team knew about releases in time and could connect the dots when something went wrong. We already tripped over this once, when the infrastructure team shipped sensitive code and support had no idea, so a customer issue took much longer to sort out (details <https://adapty-team.slack.com/archives/C035WAT083Y/p1782555171158509|here>). I’m with <@U05QELDHUUX> and suggest we bring back the practice of announcing releases. Let’s use the old message format (like <https://adapty-team.slack.com/archives/C04SY70QZ0T/p1782447994191469|this>), and also tag the messages with `#released` at the start.

<@U08EVBTE69E> <@U07J9LKBQ5U> <@U03J8UXUDPF> <@U03K1BGS464> Folks, please pick this up too.

entries.name: hey team,
entries.message:
hey team,

need some help with Readability who is evaluating RC needs some answers and ready to sign now if we can give the right AND ACCURATE responses.

i go into more detail but overall they feel like the onboarding is a incomplete product, and that RC, has a great onboarding and paywall builder in comparison to us. this goes against all internal dialogue so i hope we can turn these questions into feedback and action items.

quick background:

• legacy reading/education app
• 21k+ 5-star reviews
• ~$250k MRR today
• existing FunnelFox customer
• evaluating Adapty vs RevenueCat (RC is "more mature and has a better onboarding builder" 
• expects to scale roughly 2-2.5x before the end of 2026
they are already invested in FunnelFox and want to stay in our ecosystem if we can confidently answer a few questions. details all below:

<@U9HDNS9S4>

• does the new onboarding builder support sign in/sign up with Apple, Google, Facebook, email, and existing account login?
• can they place authentication both before and after the paywall within the onboarding flow?
• can they make API calls during onboarding and write/read data from their backend?
• will custom HTML/script support be available in the new onboarding builder and when?
• how confident are we that Android support for the onboarding builder ships in early July?
• what is the status and ETA for React Native integration with flow builder ?
<@U9HDNS9S4> / <@U0AGF7L13L5>

• RC has Amazon support and they sell on amazon, is this on our road map. when? 
• what is the status and ETA for Apple Retention Messaging?
they also have concerns stemming from their FunnelFox implementation and the Braintree workarounds they had to build.
need clarity on:


• entitlement management for Braintree subscriptions
• app access for Braintree subscribers
• analytics visibility
• can Braintree subscriptions be imported and used for entitlement/access management inside Adapty?
• how historical Braintree subscription data would be migrated
• engineering lift required
• known limitations
<@U08EVBTE69E>

RevenueCat was positioned as having a massive template library and a more mature onboarding platform.

they brought templates up multiple times throughout the call as a way to reduce implementation time and get to best practices faster.

• when can we realistically expect onboarding templates?
• when could we realistically promise onboarding templates for children's education/reading apps?
one additional note:

they only plan to run 3 onboarding/paywall flows initially.

if we can answer the questions above and get those first few flows stood up, I think we win this deal. PS is obviously slammed, but I don't think we need a huge engagement here to get them over the finish line.

<@U074DLWC5L7> <@U08MPLZ50NP> if we cannot have templates and SSO and everything else they need would it be possible to build 1-3 funnels and paywalls for them? this is a RC head to head and will be over 500MRR in less than 6 months.

appreciate any guidance.

cc: <@U034A27SVHC> if you would like to join the call i added you as optional

entries.message:
Hi there! I suppose sometimes core-related posts will look less like a cool new feature for customers. So, this is a story about an invisible defensive feature: the kind that hopefully no customer ever notices, because its whole purpose is to prevent bad things from happening in the background.
It was implemented and delivered a sprint ago, but I believe that late is better than never.

*What's the deal?* 
The main problem this feature revolves around is "Forwarding event loops".
Adapty allows its users to forward events into third-party systems for further processing and that's perfectly fine - many customers, especially big ones use it. entries.name: *Problem*
entries.message:
*Problem*

The <!subteam^S0ATWJA5K6Z> has identified the root cause behind our recurring incidents related to connection pool exhaustion between Odyssey and Postgres. During purchase validation, we create a lot of records (transactions, PAL, subscriptions, non-subscriptions, transaction events, and a few others). Since this operation has to be atomic, it all happens inside a single transaction / single PG connection. As a result, Postgres accumulates a lot of uncommitted row versions that stick around for quite a while, which slows the database down once the number of concurrent operations crosses a certain threshold.

There are basically two ways to address this kind of issue:
1. Reduce the number of operations running in parallel.
2. Reduce how long each operation takes.
*Solution*

We’ve moved App Store and Play Store purchase event processing to a background job (similar to how Stripe and Paddle do it) and added rate-limiting on concurrent event handling (processing metrics are available <https://grafana.adpinfra.dev/d/dramatiq-workers/dramatiq-workers?orgId=1&var-namespace=production&var-queue=purchase_app_store&var-queue=purchase_play_store&var-actor=All&from=now-15m&to=now|here>). This smooths out event handling over time and protects us from sudden spikes coming from the stores. Nothing changes on the SDK side: we still validate purchases and grant PAL on time, no delays there.

We also did a small refactor of the core transaction validation module, which cut the time a transaction stays open by around 60%.

Technical details are in this <https://gitlab.adapty.io/adapty/adapty-dashboard-api/-/merge_requests/12810|MR>.

*Risks*

If customers start complaining about delayed event delivery to their hooks (custom webhooks or raw event forwarding), or about issues with granting PAL, ping <!subteam^S09JZKWUF2N>.

entries.name: *New revenue and LTV predictions for cohorts*
entries.message:
Feature: *New revenue and LTV predictions for cohorts*
Release date: Apr 22, 2026
Affected areas: Analytics (Cohorts)

Revenue and LTV predictions for cohorts are now powered by a new model, this is the first major update since 2024. See details in the <https://adapty.io/docs/predicted-ltv-and-revenue|docs>.

What's different
The old model predicted revenue directly, without much visibility into how. The new one takes an interpretable approach: it predicts churn between renewal periods, and derives revenue/LTV from there. This means every prediction has a traceable logic behind it.

Why it's more trustworthy
The old model had a tendency to overestimate (<https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/DS-764|one>, <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/DS-748|two>, <https://adaptyio.atlassian.net/browse/ADP-5506|three>). The new model is less prone to it by design. In testing, cases with overestimates dropped by half.

Overall, we now have a simpler model that matches the previous quality in terms of median error, while making predictions interpretable and more trustworthy.

We’ll add a tooltip to the dashboard later this week to let users know about this update.

*Feature:* AdaptyMail — AI-powered email marketing for subscription apps
*Release date:* Apr 8, 2026
*Affected areas:* AdaptyMail (new product line)
*Audience:* Sales, CS, Growth teams, SDR, Marketing
*What's new*
AdaptyMail is live in Beta. A new product that generates complete lifecycle email campaigns from app store metadata using AI.

 *Core capabilities:*
 - AI analyzes app brand, category, and audience from App Store / Google Play listing
 - Generates 7–15 personalized HTML emails in under 2 minutes
 - 13 email types: Welcome → Product Discovery → Social Proof → Final Chance
 - AI-generated hero images that match the app's brand
 - 6 responsive layouts with dark mode
 - Built-in A/B testing (3–10 variants per email, automatic winner rollout)
 - Sending infrastructure included — DKIM, SPF, DMARC configured automatically on customer's domain
 - Personalized checkout links with closed-loop revenue attribution

*Pricing model:* 20% of incremental revenue only. No platform fees. No setup costs. No minimum commitment.

*Page:* <http://adapty.io/mail|adapty.io/mail> (will be changed soon :slightly_smiling_face: )

 - *73% of subscription apps* collect email addresses but never send a single lifecycle email — they lack the time, the copywriter, or the budget for Braze
 - *Top subscription apps make 4–13% of total revenue from email.* Most apps see 0%. That's money left on the table
 - AdaptyMail removes all three blockers at once: no copywriter needed, no months of setup, no unmeasurable ROI
 - Works on existing Adapty data — zero additional integration for current customers
 - Pure revenue share means zero risk for the customer: if we don't generate revenue, they pay nothing

*ICP:* Any Adapty customer (or prospect) who collects email addresses but doesn't run lifecycle email campaigns. Especially strong for teams without a dedicated email marketer or Braze/Iterable contract.

Introducing Apple Ads Manager 2.0: Market Intelligence, Smarter Automation, and More
We’ve been busy. Today we’re rolling out the biggest update to Apple Ads Manager by Adapty since launch — a set of features designed to help you spend less time managing campaigns and more time growing your app.
Here’s what’s new.



Market Intelligence: See What Your Competitors Are Bidding On
Finding the right keywords for Apple Ads has always been part science, part guesswork. You run Discovery campaigns, test broad matches, maybe check a few ASO tools — and hope for the best.
Market Intelligence changes that. Pick your competitors (or discover new ones using ASO search — just enter a relevant keyword and see who ranks organically), and we’ll show you exactly which keywords they’re running Apple Ads on, across 50+ countries.
What you can do with it:
• See competitor keyword strategies grouped by country or by app.
• Find the most contested keywords in your category — and the gaps nobody’s covering.
• Discover long-tail keywords (specific, lower-competition phrases like “budget meal planner for families”) that your competitors use but you haven’t tried yet. These often have lower CPAs and higher ROAS than popular head terms.
• Check if competitors are bidding on your brand keywords — and in which countries.
• Research a new market before you launch there. See what works for local competitors before spending a dollar.
• Export everything to CSV or add keywords directly to your campaigns from the same screen.
Think of it as a free alternative to running Discovery campaigns for keyword research. Instead of spending budget to find what works, look at what’s already working for your competitors and start from there.


New Automation Actions: Full Keyword Lifecycle on Autopilot
Rule-based automation just got a lot more powerful. Until now, you could change bids automatically. Now you can manage the entire keyword lifecycle.
New actions for targeting keywords:
• Enable Keyword — automatically re-enable a paused keyword when conditions are met. Perfect for cases where you paused a keyword too early, but its D31 or D61 ROAS (available through Adapty’s cohort data) turns out to be great. Give good keywords a second chance — backed by data.
• Pause Keyword — automatically pause keywords that underperform. Set your threshold (e.g., spend > $100 with zero conversions) and let the system handle it. No more budget waste going unnoticed over weekends.
• Add as Keyword to… — copy a keyword to another ad group with your preferred bid and match type. Automate your testing-to-scaling pipeline: when a keyword hits your CPA target in a test campaign, move it to your scale campaign automatically.
• Add as Negative Keyword to… — negate keywords at the ad group or campaign level. Keep your Discovery and Max Conversion campaigns clean by auto-negating any keyword that’s already running as an exact match elsewhere.
New action for search terms:
• Add as Negative Keyword to… — automatically negate irrelevant or wasteful search terms from Discovery and Max Conversion campaigns. Set a rule (e.g., 50+ impressions and 0 taps) and stop paying for traffic that doesn’t convert.
These actions work across all your campaigns and countries. Set the rules once — the system runs 24/7.


Bid History on Keyword Charts
Ever changed a bid and wondered what happened next? Now you don’t have to guess.
The keyword performance chart shows a marker at every point where the CPT bid was changed, along with the exact bid amount. You can visually correlate bid changes with shifts in impressions, taps, CPA, and other metrics — all on one chart.
This is especially useful when multiple team members manage the same campaigns. The chart becomes your changelog: every bid change is visible, and its impact is clear.



New Overview Page
We added a dedicated Overview page that shows all your key metrics at a glance — spend, revenue, ROAS, impressions, CPM, taps, CPT, TTR, downloads, CPA, and download rate — each with a daily trend chart.
You can customize which metrics are shown and in what order, filter by a specific app or view your entire account, and switch between time ranges. It’s the “how are things going?” dashboard that takes 5 seconds to read — and it’s the page Apple should have built but didn’t.



Coming Soon: CPP A/B Testing — Beta Sign-Up Is Open
One more thing. We’re about to launch a feature we’ve been working on for a while: Custom Product Page A/B Testing for Apple Ads.
Apple now lets you create up to 70 Custom Product Pages per app — alternative versions of your App Store page with different screenshots, descriptions, and previews. The problem? There’s no native way to test which one actually converts better for your ads.
CPP A/B Testing in Ads Manager solves this. Assign multiple product pages to the same keywords, split traffic automatically, and let the system find a winner with 90%+ statistical confidence. And here’s what makes our approach different: we don’t just measure which page gets more downloads — we measure which page drives the best ROAS by connecting to Adapty’s revenue data. Because a page that converts more installs isn’t always the page that converts more paying users.
We’re currently running the feature in production and opening beta access next week. If you want early access, reach out to your account manager or reply to this email — we’ll add you to the list.

And There’s More Coming
We have a packed roadmap with major features already in the pipeline. This is just the beginning of the 2.0 era — stay tuned for the next updates.

Ready to try it? All features are live in your Apple Ads Manager dashboard. Log in and explore what’s new. Questions or feedback? Reach out to your account manager or contact us at <mailto:support@adapty.io|support@adapty.io>.
